bullet_points: Load returns.csv, market_cap.csv, book_to_market.csv, factors.csv, and true_betas.csv.
Create a multi-index DataFrame (Time, Ticker) containing all stock-level data.
Verify data integrity and handle any missing values or alignment issues.
Save the cleaned panel as a single file for subsequent steps.
sub_tasks.sub_task: Load all provided CSV files, align them into a unified panel indexed by time and ticker, and standardize the factor returns to monthly frequency.

bullet_points: Use the residual covariance matrix (estimated from full-sample OLS residuals against the four factors) as the Σ matrix in the projection formula w = Σ^-1β(β'Σ^-1β)^-1.
Compute Ideal FMP returns as the dot product of time-invariant weights with the full time-series of stock returns.
Define IR as the annualized mean divided by the annualized standard deviation of the FMP return series.
Save the Ideal IR values to a results file.
sub_tasks.sub_task: Construct the "Ideal FMP" using ground-truth loadings and calculate baseline performance metrics.

bullet_points: Use a 36-month rolling window ending at t-1 to estimate both β̂ and the residual covariance matrix.
Apply weights to month t returns.
Ensure the out-of-sample FMP return series begins at month 37.
Compute the annualized IR for the sample-estimated FMP over the out-of-sample period (months 37-120) and evaluate the Ideal FMP over the same window for fair comparison.
sub_tasks.sub_task: Implement a 36-month rolling-window estimation to generate time-varying factor loadings (β̂) and construct Sample-Estimated FMPs.

bullet_points: Iterate N from 10 to 50 in increments of 5.
Stratify random ticker sampling to preserve small/large-cap and value/growth proportions proportionally to N.
Perform 500 random iterations per N, using the out-of-sample window (months 37-120) consistently.
Save the distribution of IRs for each N and each factor.
sub_tasks.sub_task: Systematically vary the cross-sectional breadth (N) and compute performance distributions.

bullet_points: Calculate mean IR decay (Ideal IR - Sample IR) and apply Newey-West standard errors (lag = integer part of 4*(T/100)^(2/9)).
Identify "critical breadth" threshold for each factor as the smallest N where the Newey-West t-statistic of the mean FMP return exceeds 1.96.
Produce a multi-panel figure: (a) IR ratio decay curves with shaded inter-quartile ranges, (b) mean annualized factor premium with 95% confidence bands vs N.
Print and save a summary table (CSV) containing Ideal IR, mean Sample IR, IR ratio, mean premium, SE, t-stat, and critical breadth.
sub_tasks.sub_task: Quantify IR decay, identify statistical thresholds, and generate the final multi-panel figure.

bullet_points: Explicitly reference numerical values from the summary table (Ideal IR, critical thresholds, IR ratios at N=50 vs N=10).
Discuss the theoretical relationship between the noise-to-signal ratio (idiosyncratic volatility / factor premium) and the observed critical breadth.
Contrast the recovery challenge of the SMB factor (negative Sharpe) against the WML factor (high Sharpe).
Synthesize findings on the minimum cross-sectional breadth required for reliable factor premium recovery.
